audit_status.review_note: Communal defeat, ancestral memory, innocence protest, shame, slaughter, and divine hiddenness.

verses.restored: We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

familiar.text: We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

modern.text: We have heard with our ears, O God; our fathers have told us the work You did in their days, in the days of old.

original.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ לִבְנֵי קֹ֬רַח מַשְׂכִּֽיל אֱלֹהִ֤ים בְּאָזְנֵ֬ינוּ שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ לָ֑נוּ פֹּ֥עַל פָּעַ֥לְתָּ בִֽ֝ימֵיהֶ֗ם בִּ֣ימֵי קֶֽדֶם

verses.restored: How thou didst drive out the nations with thy hand, and plantedst them; how thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.

familiar.text: How thou didst drive out the heathen with thy hand, and plantedst them; how thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.

modern.text: With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out.

original.text: אַתָּ֤ה יָדְךָ֡ גּוֹיִ֣ם ה֭וֹרַשְׁתָּ וַתִּטָּעֵ֑ם תָּרַ֥ע לְ֝אֻמִּ֗ים וַֽתְּשַׁלְּחֵֽם

verses.restored: For they got not the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them: but thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favour to them.

familiar.text: For they got not the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them: but thy right hand, and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou hadst a favour unto them.

modern.text: For it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory. It was by Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You favored them.

original.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֪א בְחַרְבָּ֡ם יָ֥רְשׁוּ אָ֗רֶץ וּזְרוֹעָם֮ לֹא הוֹשִׁ֪יעָ֫ה לָּ֥מוֹ כִּֽי יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וּ֭זְרוֹעֲךָ וְא֥וֹר פָּנֶ֗יךָ כִּ֣י רְצִיתָֽם

verses.restored: Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob.

familiar.text: Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob.

modern.text: You are my King, O God, who ordains victories for Jacob.

original.text: אַתָּה ה֣וּא מַלְכִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים צַ֝וֵּ֗ה יְשׁוּע֥וֹת יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.

familiar.text: Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.

modern.text: Through You we repel our foes; through Your name we trample our enemies.

original.text: בְּ֭ךָ צָרֵ֣ינוּ נְנַגֵּ֑חַ בְּ֝שִׁמְךָ֗ נָב֥וּס קָמֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: For I will not trust in my bow, neither shall my sword save me.

familiar.text: For I will not trust in my bow, neither shall my sword save me.

modern.text: For I do not trust in my bow, nor does my sword save me.

original.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְקַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶבְטָ֑ח וְ֝חַרְבִּ֗י לֹ֣א תוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי

verses.restored: But thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put them to shame that hated us.

familiar.text: But thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put them to shame that hated us.

modern.text: For You save us from our enemies; You put those who hate us to shame.

original.text: כִּ֣י ה֭וֹשַׁעְתָּנוּ מִצָּרֵ֑ינוּ וּמְשַׂנְאֵ֥ינוּ הֱבִישֽׁוֹתָ

verses.restored: In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. Selah.

familiar.text: In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. Selah.

modern.text: In God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever. Selah

original.text: בֵּֽ֭אלֹהִים הִלַּלְ֣נוּ כָל הַיּ֑וֹם וְשִׁמְךָ֓ לְעוֹלָ֖ם נוֹדֶ֣ה סֶֽלָה

verses.restored: But thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and goest not forth with our armies.

familiar.text: But thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and goest not forth with our armies.

modern.text: But You have rejected and humbled us; You no longer go forth with our armies.

original.text: אַף זָ֭נַחְתָּ וַתַּכְלִימֵ֑נוּ וְלֹא תֵ֝צֵ֗א בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they which hate us spoil for themselves.

familiar.text: Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy: and they which hate us spoil for themselves.

modern.text: You have made us retreat from the foe, and those who hate us have plundered us.

original.text: תְּשִׁיבֵ֣נוּ אָ֭חוֹר מִנִּי צָ֑ר וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֵ֗ינוּ שָׁ֣סוּ לָֽמוֹ

verses.restored: Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the nations.

familiar.text: Thou hast given us like sheep appointed for meat; and hast scattered us among the heathen.

modern.text: You have given us up as sheep to be devoured; You have scattered us among the nations.

original.text: תִּ֭תְּנֵנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן מַאֲכָ֑ל וּ֝בַגּוֹיִ֗ם זֵרִיתָֽנוּ

verses.restored: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.

familiar.text: Thou sellest thy people for nought, and dost not increase thy wealth by their price.

modern.text: You sell Your people for nothing; no profit do You gain from their sale.

original.text: תִּמְכֹּֽר עַמְּךָ֥ בְלֹא ה֑וֹן וְלֹ֥א רִ֝בִּ֗יתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.

familiar.text: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.

modern.text: You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us.

original.text: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ חֶ֭רְפָּה לִשְׁכֵנֵ֑ינוּ לַ֥עַג וָ֝קֶ֗לֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: Thou makest us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the people.

familiar.text: Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.

modern.text: You have made us a byword among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples.

original.text: תְּשִׂימֵ֣נוּ מָ֭שָׁל בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם מְנֽוֹד רֹ֝֗אשׁ בַּל אֻמִּֽים

verses.restored: My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,

familiar.text: My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,

modern.text: All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame has covered my face,

original.text: כָּל הַ֭יּוֹם כְּלִמָּתִ֣י נֶגְדִּ֑י וּבֹ֖שֶׁת פָּנַ֣י כִּסָּֽתְנִי

verses.restored: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger.

familiar.text: For the voice of him that reproacheth and blasphemeth; by reason of the enemy and avenger.

modern.text: at the voice of the scorner and reviler, because of the enemy, bent on revenge.

original.text: מִ֭קּוֹל מְחָרֵ֣ף וּמְגַדֵּ֑ף מִפְּנֵ֥י א֝וֹיֵ֗ב וּמִתְנַקֵּֽם

verses.restored: All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant.

familiar.text: All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant.

modern.text: All this has come upon us, though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant.

original.text: כָּל זֹ֣את בָּ֭אַתְנוּ וְלֹ֣א שְׁכַחֲנ֑וּךָ וְלֹֽא שִׁ֝קַּ֗רְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way;

familiar.text: Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way;

modern.text: Our hearts have not turned back; our steps have not strayed from Your path.

original.text: לֹא נָס֣וֹג אָח֣וֹר לִבֵּ֑נוּ וַתֵּ֥ט אֲשֻׁרֵ֗ינוּ מִנִּ֥י אָרְחֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.

familiar.text: Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.

modern.text: But You have crushed us in the lair of jackals; You have covered us with deepest darkness.

original.text: כִּ֣י דִ֭כִּיתָנוּ בִּמְק֣וֹם תַּנִּ֑ים וַתְּכַ֖ס עָלֵ֣ינוּ בְצַלְמָֽוֶת

verses.restored: If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god;

familiar.text: If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a strange god;

modern.text: If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a foreign god,

original.text: אִם שָׁ֭כַחְנוּ שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַנִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּ֝פֵּ֗ינוּ לְאֵ֣ל זָֽר

verses.restored: Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

familiar.text: Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.

modern.text: would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart?

original.text: הֲלֹ֣א אֱ֭לֹהִים יַֽחֲקָר זֹ֑את כִּֽי ה֥וּא יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ תַּעֲלֻמ֥וֹת לֵֽב

verses.restored: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

familiar.text: Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

notes.title: For your sake we are killed all day
notes.body: This communal lament describes innocent suffering rather than deserved punishment. Paul later cites it in Romans 8:36; neither context permits blaming victims for persecution.

modern.text: Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.

original.text: כִּֽי עָ֭לֶיךָ הֹרַ֣גְנוּ כָל הַיּ֑וֹם נֶ֝חְשַׁ֗בְנוּ כְּצֹ֣אן טִבְחָֽה

verses.restored: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.

familiar.text: Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever.

modern.text: Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever.

original.text: ע֤וּרָה לָ֖מָּה תִישַׁ֥ן אֲדֹנָ֑י הָ֝קִ֗יצָה אַל תִּזְנַ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח

verses.restored: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?

familiar.text: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?

modern.text: Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and oppression?

original.text: לָֽמָּה פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר תִּשְׁכַּ֖ח עָנְיֵ֣נוּ וְֽלַחֲצֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth to the earth.

familiar.text: For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the earth.

modern.text: For our soul has sunk to the dust; our bodies cling to the earth.

original.text: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה לֶעָפָ֣ר נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ דָּבְקָ֖ה לָאָ֣רֶץ בִּטְנֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies’ sake.

familiar.text: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies’ sake.

modern.text: Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion.

original.text: ק֭וּמָֽה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לָּ֑נוּ וּ֝פְדֵ֗נוּ לְמַ֣עַן חַסְדֶּֽךָ

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: The psalm explicitly resists victim-blaming: suffering is not proof of communal guilt. Violent defeat must not justify holy war in response.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
